main_text.p: lem, tum sensitivum: & inter voluntatem, quæ appetitus rationalis dicitur.
Claudatur prima pars per hæc πογίσματα.
I. Hominem ergo solum ratione & voluntate uti.

II. Solius hominis esse virtutem tum ἀγαθ-νομικῶ, tum φυσικῶ: quia solus habet utriusq; subjecta: & principia scientiarum & artium capax: docere ac discere potest: Solus etiam habet organa: intellectum, sermonem, electionem, civitatem, leges, &c.

III. Solus homo contemplatur, agnoscit, miratur, reveretur, celebrat Deum: ex fine suo. Vide quomodo Lactantius lib.3. cap. 10. ostendat religionem solam propriam esse hominis: cum in ceteris omnibus bruta homini quodammodo communicare videantur. Ex notitiis item naturalib. testimonio Ciceronis; ex corporis figura: Vide rursus Lactantium lib.7.cap.4.5.8.9.
main_text.head: De Secundo.
main_text.p: Revocentur omnia argumenta, quibus ratio brutis vendicari posse videtur ad duas classes. 1. sit eorum, quæ intelligentiam & voluntatem. II. eorum quæ virtutem brutis inesse docent.
main_text.head: Argumentum pro ratione & voluntate brutorum.

page.notes: The Greek words in section II and the Greek heading in section I were transcribed as best as legible; the Greek forms (ἀγαθ-/νομικῶ, φυσικῶ, πογίσματα) are uncertain and may be misread. The phrase "quæ intelligentiam & voluntatem. II." is a near-reading of a line with a printed numeral; the spacing and numbering are doubtful. The line "Quic-" at the foot is a catchword/line-end and is also given in main_text; it may belong only to the catchword. Page furniture: page number "74" and running head "EXERCITAT. PHILOSOPH." are read from the printed head.
